messages.author: b342bb9f77f5c97a
messages.subject: težave z barchart(lattice)
parts:
Pozdravljeni!

Narisati želim T-RFLP profile (kar koli že to je) hkrati za različne
restrikcijske encime z barchart (izvedva xyplot iz paketa lattice).
Imam težave z x-osjo, ki nekako noče prikazovati tistega, kar želim
(itak). Podatki (dolžine fragmentov) so med 0 in 1600, na grafu pa je
iz neznanega razloga privzeta dolžina osi x med 0 in ~250. Na to os so
potem nanizani vsi moji podatki s pravilnimi frekvencami (os y),
vendar so razdalje na osi x med njimi popačene. Enako je problem z
oznakami osi x, ker napisi (labels) ne prikazujejo dejanskih vrednosti
podatkov (0-1600) pač pa tisto arbitrarno skalo (0-250). Ali ima kdo
kakšno idejo, zakaj je temu tako?

(ang.: I wish to draw T-RFLP profiles (lots of them on a single plot)
with barchart (package lattice). X-axis, however, refuses to behave as
expected: my data is between 0 and 1600, however, x-axis appears to be
skewed and plots all my data on an arbitrary scale from 0-250. No
wonder there is also the problem of labels, which show arbitrary
values rather than the values of actual data. Any ideas?)

Tole sem vpisal:

> CV4<-read.table("clipboard", header=TRUE, dec=",", sep="\t")
> with(CV4, barchart(freq~fl|encim, horizontal=FALSE, layout=c(1,8),
main="in silico T-RFLP", xlab="dolžina fragmenta", ylab="frekvenca
fragmentov v bazi", scales=list(x=list(relation="same"))))

I know scales (relation="same") is the default value, but I tried it
all the same...

But that aside, let me just say that it's a wonderful thing that so
many people have joined the R-initiative and many thanks to the
initiators!

(S)mejte se,
Luka

messages.author: 08f3062efe0fd1ca
messages.subject: Re: [Rkoholiki] težave z barchart(lattice)
parts:
Your plot is not working because you're trying to use a barchart for something that a histogram would be needed. If I understand this correctly, barchart function changes the ff into characters, but you want frequencies. If you plot a histogram of CV4$fl you will notice that y axis is about 200, which is about the length of x axis you get with the limited axis in your example.

Here is my code for this lattice plot:

library(plyr) #I need this package to use file.choose() function - you can always use File -> Load Workspace.
load(file.choose()) #I am loading the workspace Luka sent me (.RData)
library(lattice) #we need to load the lattice library to have a faceting plot

#We use with() function to specify which data.frame we are using. The alternative is to use attach() but it can get (really) messy.
We could use histogram() but I find it faster to coarse it into a histogram-like-monster with type="h". If anyone knows how to coarse histogram's bars into lines, I would much appreciate it.
with(CV4, {
xyplot(ff~fl | encim,
horizontal=F, layout=c(2,7), lwd=0.1, type="h")})

We could use histogram() but I find it faster to coarse it into a histogram-like-monster with type="h". If anyone knows how to coarse histogram's bars into lines, I would much appreciate it.

This is the product of the above code, which is pretty close to what Luka had in mind with coplot().

To help with the solving process, if you feel attaching your data is neccessary to reproduce your problem, feel free to attach your workspace (File -> Save Workspace and give it an informative name). I would recommend attaching files is by visiting the Anonimni Rkoholiki google groups page and uploading your file to the server directly. You can attach the link in your email which will keep the size of your emails down.

Cheereo,
Roman
